>       "description": "<p>Introducing the Simple Design System: A UI kit built by Figma to help you get started faster using pre-built examples and components. This library covers Figma’s best practices for building a basic design system, and includes a full range of resources to enable core design use cases – like designing for web, mobile, and more.</p><p><br></p><p>Key features include:</p><p><br></p><ol><li data-list=\"bullet\">Examples – Full screen mockups that can be inserted into your file to go from blank page to polished designs quickly</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">400+ components, backed by code (Code Connect available on paid plans only)</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Styles and variables support, including light and dark mode</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Commonly used icons</li></ol><p><br></p><p>The code is available to view on Figma's Github account: <a href=\"https://github.com/figma/sds\" rel=\"noreferrer noopener nofollow ugc\" target=\"_blank\">https://github.com/figma/sds</a>. The repository contains icons, variables, and components as well as useful scripts for getting started with Code Connect.</p><p><br></p><p>Figma's Simple Design System UI Kit is licensed by Figma under CC BY 4.0.</p><p><br></p><p>--</p><p><br></p><h2><strong>Changelog</strong></h2><p><br></p><p>📆 <strong>Tuesday March 12 2026</strong></p><p><code><strong>Added</strong></code></p><ol><li data-list=\"bullet\">Example page template with slot for main content</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Form (Slot) – Vanilla container for adding form elements inside</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Hero (Slot) – Empty responsive hero section with slot container</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Card (Slot) – Empty card container with slot for main content</li></ol><p><br></p><p><code><strong>Fixed</strong></code></p><ol><li data-list=\"bullet\">Removed stray annotations on Example page</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Text Link List – Fixed bug with auto layout on Text Strong instance’s width</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Text List – Fixed bug with auto layout on Text Strong instance’s width</li></ol><p><br></p><p><code><strong>Changed</strong></code></p><ol><li data-list=\"bullet\">Accordion – Child items have been wrapped in a Slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">AI Chat – Components have been refactored to add Slots to repeatable content • opportunities</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Avatar Group – Avatars wrapped in a Slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Card – Converted Body to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Dialog – A new auto layout frame has been added to the dialog body, and converted to a slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Menu – A new auto layout frame is wrapping the content, and has been converted to a slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Navigation Pill List – Wrapped menu items in a slot auto layout frame</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Pagination List – Page list components wrapped in new auto layout frame and converted to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Tabs – Items been wrapped in a new auto layout frame, which has been converted to a Slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Tag Toggle Group – Tags have been wrapped in a new auto layout frame, which has been converted to a Slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Tooltip – Wrapped body content in a new Slot autolayout frame</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Text Link List – Added slot auto layout wrapper to list items</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Text List – Added slot auto layout wrapper to list items</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Footer – Wrapped title section and menu item section in slots</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Panel Image Content – Text Content Flow converted to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Panel Image Content Reverse – Text Content Flow converted to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Card Grid Pricing – Card Grid converted to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Card Grid Icon – Cards converted to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Card Grid Image – Wrapped Card auto layout frames in a new auto layout frame and converted to a slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Card Grid Content List – Converted Cards to a slot container</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Card Grid Testimonials – Converted Cards to a slot container</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Page Product – Converted Column to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Page Product Results – Added new auto layout frame inside Filter Menu and converted to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Page Product Results – Converted Card Grid to slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Navigation Button List – Wrapped menu items in slot</li><li data-list=\"bullet\">Examples – Removed blank “link” menu item from header</li></ol><h2><br></h2><p><strong>📆 Monday November 17 2025</strong></p><p><code><strong>Added</strong></code></p><ol><li data-list=\"ordered\">Date Input Field component</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Date Picker Field component</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Calendar component</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">AI Chat Box component</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">AI Chat Example page</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Blue primitive ramp</li></ol><p><br></p><p><code><strong>Fixed</strong></code></p><ol><li data-list=\"ordered\">Restored previously unpublished Button component</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Warning tag is using wrong icon variable</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Warning tag secondary is using wrong background fill variable</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Examples/Contact Us used the wrong background variable</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Change Slider to hug and add min-width of 80</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Change textarea min-width from 240 to 120</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Change Checkbox from fixed to hug and add min-width of 120 to children</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Checkbox is using a ghost variable for the border</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Change Radio from fixed to hug and add min-width of 120 to children</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Change Search from fixed to min-width 120</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Change Switch from fixed to min-width 120</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Textarea disabled border is using a ghost value</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Select field disabled state is not using a variable</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Input field disabled state is not using a variable</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Date field disabled state is not using a variable</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Search field disabled state is not using a variable</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Remove Brand B Light from Color collection</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Change disabled colors from Brand to Gray primitives</li></ol><p><br></p><p><code><strong>Changed</strong></code></p><ol><li data-list=\"ordered\">Input Fields variants have been rearranged. Now types are arranged horizontally, and variations vertically</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Inputs page documentation rearranged to be more grid-like</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Default state of Search Value Type property renamed to Filled</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Default variant of Search component changed to Placeholder, Default</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Reorganised Sections page</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Replace min-width on inputs with 120 instead of 240</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Change Select from fixed to hug</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Un-hide text components</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Document hidden text components, explaining when and why they are used</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Add auto layout to bullet list text components</li><li data-list=\"ordered\">Detached all icon variants, split them into sections based on size</li></ol><h2><br></h2><p>📆 June 3 2025</p><p><code><strong>Fixed</strong></code></p><ol><li data-list=\"ordered\">Restored previously unpublished Button component</li></ol>",

> Ab main Figma canvas me ek complete product blueprint build kar raha hoon. Yeh high-level wireframes honge: user ko app ka full flow samajh aa jaye, aur dev/design validation ke liye screens ka structure bhi ready rahe.

}\nfunction text(parent,str,x,y,w,size=16,style='Regular',color=C.ink,line=1.28){\n  const t = figma.createText(); t.name = str.slice(0,40); t.x=x; t.y=y; t.fontName={family:'Inter',style}; t.fontSize=size; t.lineHeight={unit:'PERCENT', value: line*100}; t.fills=solid(color); t.characters=str; t.textAutoResize='HEIGHT'; t.resize(w, t.height); parent.appendChild(t); createdNodeIds.push(t.id); return t;\n}\nfunction pill(parent,label,x,y,fill=C.blueSoft,color=C.blue,w=90){\n  rect(parent,'Pill '+label,x,y,w,30,fill,15);\n  text(parent,label,x+14,y+7,w-28,12,'Semi Bold',color,1.1);\n}\nfunction card(parent,name,x,y,w,h,title,body,accent=C.blue){\n  rect(parent,name,x,y,w,h,C.surface,16,C.line);\n  rect(parent,'Accent',x+18,y+18,8,32,accent,4);\n  text(parent,title,x+38,y+16,w-56,18,'Semi Bold',C.ink,1.15);\n  text(parent,body,x+38,y+50,w-56,13,'Regular',C.muted,1.35);\n}\nfunction metric(parent,x,y,w,label,value,sub,color=C.blue){\n  rect(parent,'Metric '+label,x,y,w,112,C.surface,16,C.line);\n  text(parent,label,x+18,y+16,w-36,12,'Medium',C.muted,1.1);\n  text(parent,value,x+18,y+38,w-36,30,'Bold',C.ink,1.05);\n  text(parent,sub,x+18,y+78,w-36,12,'Regular',color,1.15);\n}\nfunction nav(parent,active){\n  rect(parent,'Top nav',350,24,740,64,C.surface,32,C.line);\n  text(parent,'AdvocateAssistant',382,44,160,16,'Bold',C.ink,1);\n  const items=['Home','Chat','Clients','Drafts','Research']; let x=565;\n  for(const item of items){\n    if(item===active){ rect(parent,'Active '+item,x-12,34,88,44,C.ink,22); text(parent,item,x+5,47,60,14,'Semi Bold',C.surface,1); }\n    else text(parent,item,x+2,47,70,14,'Medium',C.ink,1);\n    x+=100;\n  }\n  rect(parent,'Avatar',1018,42,28,28,C.slateSoft,14,C.line);\n}\nfunction screen(title,active,x,y){\n  const s=frame(title,x,y,1440,900,C.bg,0);\n  nav(s,active);\n  text(s,title,90,118,520,34,'Bold',C.ink,1.1);\n  return s;\n}\n\n// Cover and product map\nconst cover = frame('00 Product Blueprint',0,0,1440,900,C.bg,0);\ntext(cover,'AdvocateAssistant',80,60,520,52,'Bold',C.ink,1.05);\ntext(cover,'Matter-aware AI workspace for advocates: clients, cases, chat, research, drafts, scenarios, court data, and citation-backed answers.',84,126,820,22,'Regular',C.muted,1.35);\npill(cover,'Home',86,190,C.blueSoft,C.blue,82); > in our equtiynav , we are using postgres database , so can we use supabase for our this advocate project , dono same he hoga right ? supabase ke andar bhi to postgres he rehta hai

<details><summary>2 previous messages</summary>

> Supabase wale decision me database, auth, storage, realtime, security sab touch hota hai, so main Supabase skill load karke answer ko grounded rakh raha hoon.
>
> <details><summary>Searched the web</summary>
>
> <details><summary>Searched the web</summary>

> - Searched the web for `Supabase Postgres database platform official docs PostgreSQL`
>
> </details>
>

</details>

Haan, **Supabase use kar sakte ho**, and haan core level pe Supabase ke andar **Postgres hi hota hai**. Supabase docs ke according every project gets a full Postgres database, “not a Postgres abstraction,” so EquityNav me jo Postgres thinking hai, woh Advocate project me Supabase par mostly map ho jayegi. ([supabase.com](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview?utm_source=openai))

But ek important nuance:

```text
Postgres = database
Supabase = Postgres + Auth + Storage + APIs + Realtime + Edge Functions + Vector options
```

Supabase officially Postgres database ke saath Auth, Storage, Realtime, Edge Functions, and Vector embeddings bhi provide karta hai. ([supabase.com](https://supabase.com/docs?utm_source=openai))

**Advocate Project Ke Liye Supabase Useful Hoga**
Especially because humare app me ye sab chahiye:

```text
Advocates/users
Clients
Cases/matters
Documents metadata
Chat sessions
Drafts
Research history
Scenario runs
Citations
Action items
Hearings/deadlines
```

Ye sab relational data hai, so Postgres perfect fit hai.

**Documents Ke Liye**
Legal documents PDF/DOCX/image files ko direct DB me nahi daalenge. Supabase Storage use kar sakte hain, aur DB me metadata:

```text
document_id
case_id
file_url/path
document_type
extracted_text
summary
uploaded_by
created_at
```

Supabase Storage Postgres/RLS policies ke saath access control support karta hai. ([supabase.com](https://supabase.com/storage?utm_source=openai))

**Security Important Hai**
Legal app me client/case data sensitive hoga. Supabase use karte hue hume strict RLS lagani hogi:

```text
Advocate sirf apne clients/cases dekh sake
Team member sirf assigned matters dekh sake
Service role frontend me kabhi expose na ho
Documents per-case secured hon
Audit logs maintain hon
```

Supabase docs bhi RLS ko important bolti hain for securing data when tables are exposed to app/client access. ([supabase.com](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview?utm_source=openai))

**Can We Reuse EquityNav Thinking?**
Yes.

EquityNav:

```text
User -> Client -> Grant -> Scenario -> Chat
```

Advocate app:

```text
Advocate -> Client -> Case/Matter -> Scenario -> Chat/Draft/Research
```

Database design ka pattern same rahega. Bas domain objects change honge.

**My Recommendation**
Haan, AdvocateAssistant ke liye Supabase use karna good idea hai, especially MVP ke liye. It gives us Postgres plus auth/storage faster.

But main ye karunga:

```text
Supabase Postgres = app data
Supabase Storage = uploaded legal documents
Supabase Auth = advocate/team login
Vector search = either Supabase pgvector for MVP or separate vector DB later
```

Final answer: **Yes, Supabase is a good choice. Same Postgres foundation hai, but extra backend features milte hain. Legal app ke liye bas RLS/security/data isolation ko first-class banana padega.**

Haan, bilkul. Humko AdvocateAssistant me bhi **chat upload flow** dena chahiye jaha user PDF, draft, order, notice, FIR, sale deed, judgment, DOCX, image etc. upload karke usi chat me question puch sake.

Core idea:

```text
User uploads document in chat
-> app processes it
-> document text/facts extract karta hai
-> document ko client/case se attach karta hai, if selected
-> user ke question ka answer document + legal RAG + citations ke basis pe deta hai
```

**Chat Upload Modes**
**1. Without Client/Case**
User sirf research ya document analysis ke liye upload kare:

```text
Upload: Supreme Court judgment PDF
Question: Is judgment ka ratio batao aur useful paragraphs identify karo.
```

Output:

```text
Summary
Key legal principle
Important paragraphs
How to cite it
Related cases to search
```

**2. With Client/Case Attached**
User `@client /case` attach karke upload kare:

```text
@Rajesh /Land Dispute
Upload: sale deed + legal notice
Question: Is case me temporary injunction ke chances kya hain?
```

Output:

```text
Facts extracted from uploaded docs
Applicable law
Evidence gaps
Risks
Supporting cases
Adverse cases
Next action
Suggested draft
```

**Hum Kya Files Support Karenge**
MVP me:

```text
PDF
DOCX
TXT
Images/scanned PDFs with OCR
```

Legal app ke liye later:

```text
XLSX/CSV for billing/timeline/evidence lists
Email export files
Court order bundles
```

**Legal-Specific Processing**
EquityNav/Sellsig jaisa simple PDF chunking enough nahi hoga. Hum legal layer add karenge:

```text
Document type detection:
- FIR
- charge sheet
- sale deed
- plaint
- written statement
- court order
- judgment
- legal notice
- agreement
- affidavit
- evidence document
```

Then extraction:

```text
Parties
Important dates
Court name
Case number/CNR
Sections/Acts mentioned
Reliefs claimed
Issues
Orders/directions
Deadlines
Property details
Accused/complainant details
Witnesses/evidence
```

**Chat Me User Kya Puch Sakta Hai**
Examples:

```text
"Is PDF ka summary banao."
"Is order me court ne kya direction diya?"
"Next deadline kya hai?"
"Is draft me kya missing hai?"
"Is document se list of dates bana do."
"Is FIR ke basis pe bail grounds batao."
"Sale deed me koi weakness hai?"
"Is plaint me cause of action properly pleaded hai?"
"Opposite party ka strongest argument kya ho sakta hai?"
"Is document me kaunse sections mentioned hain?"
```

**Important Feature: Save to Case**
Upload ke baad app pooche:

```text
Save this document to:
@Rajesh /Land Dispute
Document type: Sale Deed
```

Ya user directly attach kare:

```text
@Rajesh /Land Dispute + upload file
```

Then document case file ka permanent part ban jayega.

**Answer Ka Format**
Uploaded document based answer me source references hone chahiye:

```text
Short Answer
Document Facts Used
Analysis
Relevant Extracts
Legal Research
Risks / Missing Info
Next Actions
```

Example:

```text
Short answer:
The uploaded sale deed supports title, but possession proof is still weak.

Document facts used:
- Sale deed dated 12 Feb 2025
- Property described as Plot No. 44
- Buyer: Rajesh Kumar

Missing:
- mutation record
- possession proof
- latest revenue record
```

**OCR Important Hai**
Legal documents kaafi scanned hote hain. Isliye OCR zaruri hai. Agar PDF text-based hai toh direct extraction. Agar scanned hai toh OCR.

```text
Text PDF -> direct text extraction
Scanned PDF/image -> OCR
Handwritten/poor scan -> low confidence warning
```

**MVP Me Must-Have**
Chat upload ke liye MVP:

```text
Upload PDF/DOCX
Auto-detect document type
Extract text
Summarize
Ask questions from document
Attach to client/case
Store in case documents
Use in future matter-aware chat
Cite document pages/paragraphs
```

**Advocate App Me Ye Feature Killer Hoga**
Because lawyer normally yahi karega:

```text
Upload FIR -> ask bail grounds
Upload sale deed -> ask title risk
Upload court order -> ask next step
Upload plaint -> ask weaknesses
Upload judgment -> ask ratio and citation
Upload notice -> draft reply
```

So yes, chat me upload functionality mandatory hai. It should work both as:

```text
General document chat
Matter-aware document chat
```

And every uploaded file should become reusable case memory if attached to a client/case.

> ocr ke lie hum abbyy ka use karege , qki hum hackathon mey bhi jaa rahe , toh humare lie sahi ho jayega

Haan, ABBYY OCR use karna smart move hai. Hackathon requirement bhi satisfy ho jayega, aur legal app ke liye genuinely useful bhi hoga.

Hum positioning aise rakhenge:

```text
ABBYY = legal document digitization + OCR + structured extraction
Our AI = legal reasoning + RAG + drafting + research + case assistance
```

**Where ABBYY Fits**
Chat/document upload flow me:

```text
User uploads scanned PDF/image
-> ABBYY OCR extracts clean text
-> system detects document type
-> extracts legal fields
-> saves document to case
-> AI answers questions using that document
```

**Legal Use Cases**
ABBYY se hum process kar sakte hain:

```text
Scanned FIR
Court orders
Sale deed
Agreement
Legal notice
Affidavit
Judgment PDF
Charge sheet
Evidence documents
Handwritten/printed mixed docs, where possible
```

**Why Not Directly LLM PDF?**
Agar koi puche “OCR kyun, direct LLM ko PDF kyun nahi?” answer:

```text
Legal documents often come as scanned court records, low-quality PDFs, stamps, signatures, tables, handwritten notes, and multi-page bundles. Direct LLM PDF reading is not reliable enough for legal workflows. ABBYY gives us a dedicated OCR/document processing layer that creates structured, searchable, reusable text before AI analysis.
```

**Hackathon Pitch**
For hackathon, hum bol sakte hain:

> We use ABBYY to convert messy legal PDFs and scanned court documents into clean, structured case data. Then our AI assistant uses that extracted data with legal research tools to summarize matters, find evidence gaps, prepare drafts, and answer advocate questions with citations.

This makes ABBYY a **major role**, not forced integration.

>
> Files ka output bada hai, commands abhi complete ho rahe hain. V3 ka shape clear hai: pure semantic retrieval, fast but no legal/tax taxonomy pre-filter. Ab V1/V2 complete output pull karta hoon.
>
> V1/V2/V3 ka difference clear hai: V1 most controlled but slow, V2 taxonomy pre-filter + semantic retrieval, V3 fastest pure semantic. Legal RAG me mujhe V2-style “legal taxonomy pre-filter + hybrid retrieval” strongest lag raha hai, but with separate matter-doc retrieval alongside global law retrieval.

Haan, yahi sabse important architecture decision hai. Upload/OCR alag cheez hai. **RAG corpus** wo hoga jisse app legal answers, sections, precedents, citations, arguments, drafts, scenarios sab power karega.

**Short Answer**
Humare RAG me 2 main worlds honge:

```text
1. Global Legal Knowledge
   Acts, sections, rules, judgments, precedents, court rules, templates.

2. Private Matter Knowledge
   Client/case documents, uploaded PDFs, drafts, orders, notices, FIR, sale deed, notes.
```

Dono ko mix nahi karna. Global law sab users ke liye common hoga. Private matter docs sirf us advocate/case ke liye.

**RAG Me Kya Embed Karenge**
**1. Bare Acts / Statutes**
India ke liye:

```text
BNS / IPC
BNSS / CrPC
BSA / Evidence Act
CPC
Specific Relief Act
Transfer of Property Act
Registration Act
Stamp Act
Limitation Act
NI Act
Hindu Marriage Act
Muslim personal law references
Family Courts Act
NDPS Act
Consumer Protection Act
Court Fees / State amendments
```

India Code central/state acts, rules, regulations, notifications, orders, circulars, ordinances, statutes etc. ka official repository hai, so statutes ke liye ye strong source hoga. ([indiacode.nic.in](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/?utm_source=openai))

**2. Judgments / Precedents**
Embed karna hoga:

```text
Supreme Court judgments
High Court judgments
Important tribunal judgments if needed
Landmark cases
Recent cases
```

But judgment ko random chunks me nahi. Better:

```text
case title
court
date
citation
paragraph number
legal issue
holding / ratio
relevant quoted paragraph
acts/sections mentioned
topic tags
```

Indian Kanoon API claims 3 crore+ orders, search, legal documents, fragments, metadata, and query filters, so MVP me judgment source ke liye ye practical route ho sakta hai. ([api.indiankanoon.org](https://api.indiankanoon.org/?utm_source=openai))

**3. Court Orders / Live Case Data**
eCourts-type APIs ko mostly **live tool** ki tarah use karenge, not permanent global RAG. Example:

```text
case status
hearing history
cause list
orders
parties
acts/sections
```

Agar koi order user ke case se related hai, then us order ko matter documents me save karke private matter RAG me embed karenge. eCourtsIndia API pages claim cause list search, court structure, orders, hearing/case data style workflows. ([ecourtsindia.com](https://ecourtsindia.com/api?utm_source=openai))

**4. Legal Draft Templates**
Embed/template-store:

```text
legal notice
reply notice
plaint
written statement
bail application
anticipatory bail
injunction application
maintenance petition
cheque bounce complaint
evidence affidavit
argument note
```

This helps Drafts section and chat drafting.

**5. Scenario Playbooks**
For structured scenarios:

```text
Land dispute playbook
Theft/bail playbook
Family matter playbook
Cheque bounce playbook
Injunction playbook
Limitation playbook
```

Each playbook contains:

```text
required facts
required documents
common legal issues
applicable acts
evidence checklist
risk rules
output format
draft suggestions
```

**6. Private Case Documents**
From advocate upload/ABBYY OCR:

```text
FIR
charge sheet
sale deed
agreement
court order
plaint
written statement
legal notice
reply
affidavit
judgment PDF
client notes
drafts
```

These are embedded only under:

```text
advocate_id
client_id
case_id
document_id
```

**Best RAG Approach**
For our use case, best approach is:

```text
Multi-corpus, metadata-filtered hybrid RAG + reranking + citation verification
```

Not pure semantic search only.

Why? Legal queries have exact terms:

```text
Section 37 NDPS
Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 CPC
Article 54 Limitation Act
State of Punjab v Baldev Singh
registered sale deed
mutation does not prove title
```

Pure semantic search can miss exact section/case matches. Hybrid search combines keyword/full-text search with semantic search, which is exactly better for legal retrieval. Supabase docs describe hybrid search as combining full text search and semantic search for results that are both directly and contextually relevant. ([supabase.com](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search?utm_source=openai))

If we use Supabase, `pgvector` can store embeddings inside Postgres, and Supabase has docs for pgvector as a Postgres extension for vector similarity search. ([supabase.com](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/extensions/pgvector?utm_source=openai)) If we use Qdrant, Qdrant also supports hybrid queries with dense/sparse retrieval and fusion methods like RRF/DBSF. ([qdrant.tech](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/search/hybrid-queries/?utm_source=openai))

**EquityNav Files Se Learning**
`base.py`:

```text
Tax code selection -> document selection -> page selection -> context extraction -> answer
```

Very controlled, but slow.

`base_v2.py`:

```text
Tax code selection -> document selection -> semantic retrieval -> answer
```

Best pattern for us. Replace tax code with legal issue/act/section selection.

`base_v3.py`:

```text
Pure semantic search over all documents
```

Fast, but legal domain me risky as primary path.

So AdvocateAssistant ke liye best version:

```text
base_v2 style, but legal version
```

Meaning:

```text
1. Detect jurisdiction + matter type + user intent
2. Select relevant legal domains / acts / sections
3. Retrieve from filtered statutes + judgments + matter documents
4. Hybrid search, not semantic only
5. Rerank results
6. Generate answer with citations
7. Verify citation support
```

**Attached Client/Case Flow**
User asks:

```text
@Rajesh /Land Dispute
"Can we seek temporary injunction?"
```

RAG flow:

```text
1. Pull client/case facts
2. Retrieve uploaded matter docs
3. Extract issue: temporary injunction, possession, title dispute
4. Filter global law:
   country=India
   matter_type=property
   acts=CPC, Specific Relief Act, TPA, Limitation Act
5. Retrieve precedents
6. Retrieve adverse precedents
7. Answer with case-specific analysis
```

Output:

```text
Short answer
Facts considered
Applicable law
Cases for us
Cases against us
Evidence gaps
Risk
Next action
Suggested draft
```

**Without Client/Case Flow**
User asks:

```text
"NDPS Section 37 bail ke latest cases batao."
```

Flow:

```text
1. No matter context
2. Legal research route
3. Filter: India, criminal, NDPS, Section 37
4. Search statutes + judgments + external APIs
5. Return general legal research answer
```

**What Metadata Har Chunk Me Hona Chahiye**
For statutes:

```text
country
state
act_name
section_number
section_title
chapter
version/effective_date
source_url
```

For judgments:

```text
case_title
court
bench
date
citation
paragraph_number
acts_sections
legal_issue
holding
source_url
authority_level
```

For private docs:

```text
advocate_id
client_id
case_id
document_type
page_number
extracted_text
date_detected
parties
confidence
source_file
```

**My Recommendation**
MVP me:

```text
Global RAG:
- India Code acts/sections
- curated landmark judgments
- Indian Kanoon API as external search/provider
- draft templates
- scenario playbooks

Private RAG:
- uploaded case documents via ABBYY OCR
- case notes
- drafts
- court orders
```

Do not try to ingest all Indian judgments on day one. Start with statutes + curated precedents + Indian Kanoon API/search. Then cache/embed frequently used judgments and saved research.

Final answer: **Use `base_v2` thinking, not `base_v3` as primary.** For legal, we need controlled retrieval with filters, hybrid search, reranking, and citation verification. Pure semantic search is fine for quick/simple document Q&A, but not enough for serious legal answers.

> [base.py](src/agents/retrieval/base.py) ye without rag approach hai , kya betteer rahga ye ya v2 ?

For AdvocateAssistant, **V2 better rahega**.

`base.py` wala approach technically “without vector RAG” nahi, but it is more like **LLM-controlled staged retrieval**:

```text
1. Select relevant tax/legal codes
2. Select documents
3. Select pages
4. Extract context
5. Generate answer
```

Ye controlled hai, but slow aur expensive hoga because har stage me LLM decision involved hai.

`base_v2.py` approach better balance hai:

```text
1. Select relevant legal domains / acts / sections
2. Select documents/corpus filters
3. Semantic/hybrid retrieval
4. Generate answer with citations
```

**Legal App Ke Liye Best**
Pure `base.py` type approach tab useful hai jab corpus small/structured ho aur accuracy ke liye har stage me LLM reasoning chahiye. But Indian legal corpus huge hoga:

```text
Acts
Sections
Rules
Supreme Court cases
High Court cases
Matter documents
Orders
Drafts
```

Agar har query me LLM se page/document selection karwayenge, cost aur latency high ho jayegi.

**Recommended Approach**
Use **V2 as primary**:

```text
Legal issue classifier
-> act/section/domain pre-filter
-> hybrid retrieval
-> rerank
-> answer + citations
```

And keep `base.py` style as **deep research mode**:

```text
Quick answer = V2
Deep research / high-stakes answer = base.py-like multi-stage reasoning
```

So:

```text
Default chat/research: V2
Deep Thinking / Expert Research: base.py style
Simple uploaded PDF Q&A: V3/pure semantic
```

Best final architecture:

```text
V2 = main production RAG
V1/base.py = deep legal research mode
V3 = fast document chat / quick search
```

For MVP, build V2 first. It will feel fast, scalable, and accurate enough if metadata filters + hybrid search + citation verification are strong.

<details><summary>2 previous messages</summary>

> Haan, yahi practical strategy hogi: sab kuch khud ingest karna zaruri nahi. Main quick current source check kar raha hoon taaki third-party legal/court data ko RAG ke saath kaise combine karna hai, woh cleanly bata sakoon.
>
> <details><summary>Searched the web</summary>

>
> </details>

</details>

Haan, exactly. **Hume saara legal data apne RAG me daalne ki zarurat nahi hai.** Best approach ye hoga:

```text
Core high-value data apne RAG me
+
Large external legal/court databases as tools/API
+
Important retrieved docs ko cache/embed karna
```

Matlab humara system hybrid hoga:

```text
Internal RAG = fast, curated, reliable knowledge
External APIs = huge/searchable live legal data
Matter RAG = user ke private case documents
```

**Internal RAG Me Kya Rakhenge**
Sirf wo data jo repeatedly useful hai aur jiske bina app slow/unreliable ho jayega:

```text
1. Bare Acts / sections
2. Common procedural laws
3. Curated landmark judgments
4. Scenario playbooks
5. Draft templates
6. Legal issue checklists
7. Common evidence checklists
8. User-uploaded case documents
```

Example:

```text
CPC
BNSS/CrPC
BNS/IPC
BSA/Evidence Act
Specific Relief Act
Transfer of Property Act
Registration Act
Stamp Act
Limitation Act
NI Act
NDPS Act
Family laws
```

Ye humare RAG me hone chahiye because ye har answer me frequently kaam aayenge.

**External API Tool Se Kya Karenge**
Judgment/case-law ka ocean khud ingest karne ke bajay APIs use karenge.

Example APIs:

```text
Indian Kanoon API
eCourtsIndia API
Surepass eCourts API
Kanoon.dev
LegalKart/Attestr type court APIs
```

Indian Kanoon API claims 3 crore+ orders, legal document search, filters/operators, legal documents, fragments, metadata, and enriched HTML. Ye precedent research ke liye strong candidate hai. ([api.indiankanoon.org](https://api.indiankanoon.org/?utm_source=openai))

eCourtsIndia API court/cause-list side ke liye useful ho sakta hai: cause list search, available dates, court hierarchy, case data/orders/hearings type workflows. ([ecourtsindia.com](https://ecourtsindia.com/api?utm_source=openai))

Surepass eCourts API claims nationwide court coverage with case status, court/branch details, legal sections, acts, parties, and advanced filters. ([surepass.io](https://surepass.io/ecourts-api/?utm_source=openai))

Kanoon.dev also exposes court/case objects and says it provides API access for Indian law/courts. ([docs.kanoon.dev](https://docs.kanoon.dev/?utm_source=openai))

**How It Will Work**
User asks:

```text
"NDPS Section 37 bail ke latest cases batao"
```

System:

```text
1. Internal RAG se NDPS Act Section 37 + key principles retrieve karega
2. Indian Kanoon/API tool se latest/highly relevant cases search karega
3. Results ko rerank karega
4. Important judgments ke paragraphs fetch karega
5. Answer citations ke saath dega
```

User asks attached case:

```text
@Amit /Theft Case "Bail grounds kya hain?"
```

System:

```text
1. Matter docs se FIR/order facts lega
2. Internal RAG se BNS/BNSS bail law lega
3. API se recent bail precedents search karega
4. eCourts tool se case status/order history fetch kar sakta hai
5. Answer case-specific dega
```

**Important: Retrieved API Data Ko Cache Karna**
Agar API se koi important judgment/order mila, hum usko temporary ya permanent cache kar sakte hain:

```text
First time:
API se fetch -> answer me use -> cache/save

If advocate saves it:
"Save to Research" or "Attach to Case"
-> then hum us judgment/order ko apne RAG me embed kar denge
```

This gives best of both worlds:

```text
Huge corpus ka access
+
apna fast curated memory
+
lower API cost over time
```

**Internal RAG vs API Tool**
Simple rule:

```text
Frequently used, stable, core law -> Internal RAG
Huge, changing, long-tail judgments -> API tool
Live case status/cause list/orders -> API tool
User's private docs -> Private matter RAG
Saved important cases -> Internal cached RAG
```

**Why This Is Better**
Agar hum sab judgments khud ingest karenge:

```text
data huge hoga
cost high hoga
updates maintain karna hard
citation quality/manageability hard
legal source licensing issue ho sakta hai
```

Agar sirf external API use karenge:

```text
latency high
API cost dependency
rate limit
no internal intelligence
offline/no cache issue
```

Best is middle path.

**Recommended MVP**
MVP me:

```text
Internal RAG:
- statutes/common Acts
- 100-300 landmark/curated judgments
- scenario playbooks
- draft templates
- uploaded case docs

External tools:
- Indian Kanoon for precedent search
- one eCourts/court-data provider for case status/orders/cause list
- web search optional for fresh public info
```

Then gradually:

```text
Most-used API results -> cache
Saved research -> embed
Case-specific orders -> attach to matter
Frequently cited judgments -> curated global RAG
```

So haan, tumhara thought correct hai: **jo sabse important hai wo RAG me daalo, baaki large legal database APIs as tools use karo.** This is more scalable, cheaper, and faster to build.

Haan, exactly. Hum AdvocateAssistant me **EquityNav scenario engine ka legal version** bana sakte hain.

EquityNav me:

```text
Grant -> Event Type -> Scenario Form -> Strategy File -> Tax Output
```

AdvocateAssistant me:

```text
Case/Matter -> Legal Event Type -> Scenario Form -> Strategy File -> Legal Analysis Output
```

**Core Idea**
User dropdown se event type select karega:

```text
Land Dispute
Theft / Chori
Bail
Rape / Sexual Offence
Family Matter
Cheque Bounce
Domestic Violence
Divorce / Maintenance
Property Partition
Temporary Injunction
Legal Notice Reply
```

Phir uske according scenario form open hoga. User facts/documents upload/fill karega. Then `Run Scenario`.

Behind the scenes ek strategy execute hogi:

```text
strategies/land_dispute.py
strategies/theft_bail.py
strategies/family_maintenance.py
strategies/cheque_bounce.py
strategies/temporary_injunction.py
```

Har strategy ke andar us scenario ka full workflow hoga.

**But Important Difference**
EquityNav strategy mostly numeric calculation karti hai:

```text
ordinary income
capital gain
AMT
withholding
net proceeds
```

Legal strategy deterministic number nahi degi. Legal strategy output karegi:

```text
issue matrix
applicable law
evidence gap
limitation risk
case strength
supporting precedents
adverse precedents
draft suggestions
court questions
next action checklist
```

**Legal Strategy Ka Structure**
Example: `land_dispute_strategy`

Input:

```text
client_role
property_type
claim_basis
registered_document
stamp_duty_status
possession_status
date_of_dispossession
relief_sought
uploaded_documents
court_stage
jurisdiction
```

Strategy internally:

```text
1. Validate required facts
2. Identify legal issues
3. Select applicable laws
4. Retrieve statutes from RAG
5. Search precedents via Indian Kanoon/API
6. Check uploaded documents
7. Detect evidence gaps
8. Run limitation analysis
9. Generate opponent arguments
10. Generate result report
```

Output:

```text
Case snapshot
Legal issue matrix
Applicable Acts/sections
Cases in favour
Cases against
Limitation risk
Evidence checklist
Recommended relief
Draft recommendations
Court prep questions
Next actions
```

**Example: Land Dispute Scenario**
Form fields:

```text
Client role: plaintiff/defendant
Property type
Claim basis: sale deed/inheritance/possession/agreement
Is sale deed registered?
Who has possession?
When did dispute/dispossession happen?
Mutation/revenue record available?
Relief needed: declaration/injunction/possession/specific performance
Upload: sale deed, notice, revenue record, order, site map
```

Run result:

```text
Risk: Medium-High
Primary issue: title + possession
Missing critical document: possession proof
Applicable law: TPA, Registration Act, Stamp Act, Specific Relief Act, CPC, Limitation Act
Suggested draft: temporary injunction application
Court questions: who is in possession, when cause of action arose, registered title?
```

**Example: Theft / Chori Scenario**
Form fields:

```text
Client role: accused/complainant
Sections invoked
FIR date
Arrest status
Recovery made?
CCTV/witness evidence?
Prior criminal history?
Charge-sheet filed?
Bail rejected before?
Upload FIR/order/charge sheet
```

Strategy output:

```text
Bail grounds
Weakness in prosecution case
Procedural issues
Evidence status
Relevant BNS/IPC/BNSS sections
Cases supporting bail
Cases against bail
Draft bail application points
Court questions
Next steps
```

**Example: Family Matter**
Form fields:

```text
Matter type: divorce/maintenance/custody/DV
Marriage date
Children
Income details
Allegations
Existing orders
Mediation status
Documents uploaded
```

Strategy output:

```text
Issues involved
Relief options
Maintenance risk
Evidence checklist
Settlement points
Draft petition/reply suggestions
Hearing prep
```

**Strategy File Ka Role**
Har strategy file me fixed legal workflow hoga:

```text
land_dispute.py
- required_fields
- required_documents
- applicable_law_map
- risk_rules
- tool_plan
- output_schema
- run()
```

Iska matlab har scenario predictable output dega. Chat flexible hai, scenario structured hai.

**Multiple Agents/Tools Inside Strategy**
Ek strategy ke andar ye sub-agents/tools call ho sakte hain:

```text
MatterContextAgent
DocumentAnalysisAgent
LegalRAGAgent
PrecedentSearchAgent
CourtDataAgent
LimitationAgent
EvidenceGapAgent
DraftSuggestionAgent
CitationVerifierAgent
FinalReportAgent
```

Example:

```text
land_dispute_strategy.run(input)
-> document_agent.extract_property_facts()
-> legal_rag.retrieve(["TPA", "Specific Relief Act", "CPC Order 39"])
-> precedent_agent.search("temporary injunction possession title dispute")
-> evidence_agent.check_missing_docs()
-> limitation_agent.check_dates()
-> final_agent.generate_report()
```

**Event Type vs Scenario**
Hum naming aise kar sakte hain:

```text
Event Type = Legal matter category
Scenario = Specific analysis under that category
```

Example:

```text
Event Type: Property / Land
Scenarios:
- Title + possession dispute
- Temporary injunction
- Specific performance
- Partition
- Mutation/revenue dispute
```

But MVP me simple rakho:

```text
Dropdown: Land Dispute Analyzer
```

Later nested categories bana dena.

**Recommended MVP Scenarios**
Start me 5 rakho:

```text
1. Land Dispute Analyzer
2. Theft / Bail Analyzer
3. Family Matter Analyzer
4. Cheque Bounce Analyzer
5. Temporary Injunction Analyzer
```

Maybe 6th:

```text
Legal Notice / Reply Analyzer
```

**Scenario Output Contract**
Har scenario ka output same high-level structure follow kare:

```text
1. Case Snapshot
2. Facts Used
3. Missing Facts
4. Applicable Law
5. Legal Issues
6. Supporting Authorities
7. Adverse Authorities
8. Evidence Gaps
9. Risk Assessment
10. Drafting Recommendations
11. Court Prep Questions
12. Next Action Checklist
```

This makes product consistent.

**Final Product Logic**
Chat:

```text
Ask anything, flexible.
```

Scenario:

```text
Run a guided legal playbook for common cases.
```

Drafts:

```text
Generate/edit legal documents.
```

Research:

```text
Standalone precedent/statute search.
```

So yes, tumhara idea correct hai. **EquityNav strategies folder ka legal equivalent banana should be our scenario engine.** Difference ye hai ki tax strategies calculate numbers; legal strategies orchestrate facts, documents, law, precedents, risk rules, and AI report generation.

Most recently, I’ve been working on **AbbyAdv**, an AI-powered workspace for advocates to manage clients, cases, documents, legal research, drafting, and scenario analysis.

Live/demo link: currently in MVP planning and prototype stage, no public live link yet.

My role: **Founder / Product Builder**

Key contributions:
I designed the core product concept and architecture, inspired by a CPA-client workflow system but adapted for legal practice. The product lets an advocate create clients, create multiple cases under each client, attach a client/case inside chat, upload legal documents, and ask an AI assistant context-aware questions. I also designed the structured “legal scenario” engine, where an advocate can run workflows like land dispute analysis, bail strategy, cheque bounce timeline, family matter review, or temporary injunction preparation.

The most impactful part is that AbbyAdv is not just a generic legal chatbot. It combines case management, document OCR, legal RAG, citation-backed research, drafting, and external legal data APIs into one assistant that helps advocates prepare faster while keeping final legal judgment with the lawyer.
